entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8612"/><div sID="gen14137" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8612"/>3-5. Gesenius, Maurer, &c., regard these verses as an address of the fugitive Moabites to the Jews for protection; they translate <reference osisRef="Isa.16.4">Is 16:4</reference>, "Let mine outcasts of Moab dwell with thee, Judah"; the protection will be refused by the Jews, for the pride of Moab (<reference osisRef="Isa.16.6">Is 16:6</reference>). Vitringa makes it an additional advice to Moab, besides paying tribute. Give shelter to the Jewish outcasts who take refuge in thy land (<reference osisRef="Isa.16.3">Is 16:3</reference>, <reference osisRef="Isa.16.4">4</reference>); so "mercy" will be shown thee in turn by whatever king sits on the "throne" of "David" (<reference osisRef="Isa.16.5">Is 16:5</reference>). Isaiah foresees that Moab will be too proud to pay the tribute, or conciliate Judah by sheltering its outcasts (<reference osisRef="Isa.16.6">Is 16:6</reference>); therefore judgment shall be executed. However, as Moab just before is represented as itself an outcast in Idumea, it seems incongruous that it should be called on to shelter Jewish outcasts. So that it seems rather to foretell the ruined state of Moab when its people should beg the Jews for shelter, but be refused for their pride.<div eID="gen14137" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14138" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">make ... shadow as ... night ... in ... noonday--</hi>emblem of a thick shelter from the glaring noonday heat (<reference osisRef="Isa.4.6">Is 4:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.25.4">25:4</reference>; <reference osisRef="Isa.32.2">32:2</reference>).<div eID="gen14138" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14139" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">bewray ... wandereth--</hi>Betray not the fugitive to his pursuer. <div eID="gen14139" type="x-p"/>

entries.reader_content_plain: 13. since that time-- rather, "respecting that time" [Horsley]. Barnes translates it, "formerly" in contrast to "but now" ( Is 16:14 ): heretofore former prophecies ( Ex 15:15 ; Nu 21:29 ) have been given as to Moab, of which Isaiah has given the substance: but now a definite and steady time also is fixed.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv8623"/><div sID="gen14167" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv8623"/><hi type="bold">14. three years ... hireling--</hi>Just as a hireling has his fixed term of engagement, which neither he nor his master will allow to be added to or to be taken from, so the limit within which Moab is to fall is unalterably fixed (<reference osisRef="Isa.21.16">Is 21:16</reference>). Fulfilled about the time when the Assyrians led Israel into captivity. The ruins of Elealeh, Heshbon, Medeba, Dibon, &c., still exist to confirm the inspiration of Scripture. The accurate particularity of specification of the places three thousand years ago, confirmed by modern research, is a strong testimony to the truth of prophecy. <chapter eID="Isa.16"/>
